title: Sequenced OpenAI ChatCompletions adapter preserving tool/function-call ordering and structured output fidelity
creator: Marco Liu
description: Implement an adapter that accepts requests in the OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) shape and maps them to Redwood's internal conversation/generation API while preserving: (1) streaming semantics (SSE/chunk ordering), (2) tool/function calling lifecycle and deterministic ordering, and (3) structured outputs (json/schema enforcement). The adapter must be resilient to partial reconnects, support idempotent replay of streaming fragments for clients that re-connect, and emit the telemetry fields Redwood needs for cost and latency breakdowns. This ticket covers the core mapping logic, streaming framing protocol, and a compatibility test harness. Runtime integration and canary rollout handled in follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter accepts OpenAI-style chat completion POSTs and returns responses consistent with OpenAI streaming (SSE) semantics when stream=true
Tool/function call events from OpenAI format are emitted to Redwood tooling hooks with preserved argument order and a reproducible call-id
Structured output responses (when model returns a JSON snippet) are validated against provided schema hints and invalid payloads are surfaced as structured partials rather than opaque errors
On network interruption during streaming, the adapter supports at-least-once resume by allowing reconnects with last-seen event-id and avoids duplicating final 'finish' events
End-to-end compatibility tests cover legacy clients (OpenAI SDK requests) and Redwood's console showing identical final text and tool-call invocations
Telemetry includes per-request token counts, backend model variant, latency p50/p95, and a flag marking compatibility-mode routing
Security review completed for parsing user-provided function schemas and safe deserialization
Documentation and migration notes published with usage examples and known behavioral differences
engineering_notes: Approach options considered: 1) Thin proxy that rewrites payloads and streams 1:1; 2) Stateful orchestrator that materializes KV cache and function-call state per request. Chosen: hybrid stateful proxy to surface deterministic tool-call ordering and resume. Rationale: we need per-request call-ids and controlled finalization for structured outputs.

Streaming framing: use SSE with event ids mapping to Redwood internal chunk sequence numbers. We will include both 'oa_event_id' and 'rw_seq' in each chunk metadata to support legacy clients and Redwood tracing tools.

Idempotency: clients may replay chunks after disconnect. Maintain ephemeral in-memory window per request (bounded by N seconds) and persisted minimal journal for long-running streams (only for Dedicated customers behind canary).

Tool/function calls: map OpenAI 'function_call' object to Redwood 'tool_invocation' with fields: call_id (uuid v4), sequence_index, tool_name, args_raw, args_parsed. Validate args using user-provided function schemas if present; if parsing fails, emit structured 'tool_error' event rather than failing stream.

Structured output enforcement: support schema hints in 'messages' metadata (x-schema) and run lightweight JSON schema validation; on failure, include 'structured_validation' partial with error codes and the raw content.
Telemetry: add compatibility_mode=true tag and include model.variant, backend_gpu, tokens_in, tokens_out, batching_delay_ms. Hook into existing observability pipelines via trace attributes.
progress_updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff meeting with API, runtime, and security. Agreed on hybrid stateful proxy. Action items: proto mapping, telemetry fields, security checklist.
2026-02-25: Prototype streaming harness that converts OpenAI SSE chunks to internal events. Demoed partial reconnection behavior in local tests (handled by replay window).
2026-03-02: Implemented basic function_call -> tool_invocation mapping, generating call_id and sequence_index. Added unit tests for simple tool call roundtrips.

2026-03-06: Added schema hint parsing and integrated ajv-based validation for structured outputs. Discovered an edge case with nested arrays; created follow-up task ENG-742552 to harden schema validator.
2026-03-09: Security review kickoff — identified need to sandbox deserialization of args and rate-limit function schema size. Security asked for explicit feature flagging for Private deployments.
2026-03-10: Integration tests with Redwood console telemetry passing on dev cluster. Preparing PR for initial RFC and internal review.
review_feedback: PM (Aisha Khan): Ensure behavior differences are documented; clients should not rely on event framing identifiers changing during canary.
Design (Jules Martin): Prefer human-readable chunk annotations for easier debugging in Console; keep binary payloads outside SSE events.
Runtime (Priya Desai): Concern about in-memory replay window for high throughput; recommend a capped persist option only for Dedicated customers to avoid OOM on hosted tier.
Security (Omar Ruiz): Require input-size limits for function schemas and disable arbitrary eval. Approve after adding schema size checks and safe-parser.
QE (Lina Ortega): Add fuzz tests for malformed SSE fragments and function args; include simulated reconnects in CI harness.
qa_plan: Integration test: OpenAI SDK -> adapter -> Redwood runtime with streaming enabled, verify connection resume via event-id.
Canary: enable adapter for 2% of traffic with observability flags; monitor mismatch rate against canonical Redwood responses.
Fuzzing: SSE fragmentation and malformed JSON for function args.
Load test: simulate 500 concurrent streaming clients to measure memory and replay window behavior.
